title: Quick Sampler Tricks
intro: Quick Sampler turns any sound into a playable instrument — the short route from “that noise is interesting” to “that noise is now a bassline”.

tips.t: Know the four modes and pick deliberately
tips.d: Classic plays the sample while you hold a key, the way to play a sound across the keyboard. One Shot plays from start marker to end marker on each note, good for drum loops and effects. Slice chops a sample into slices mapped to keys. Recorder captures live input as an audio recording.

src.label: Apple — Choose a Quick Sampler mode in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Slice mode with Transient detection on any break
tips.d: Load a drum loop, switch to Slice, choose Transient from the Mode pop-up menu, and each slice is mapped to its own key. Drag from the lower part of the waveform display to a software instrument track in the Tracks area to get the MIDI — the original groove, fully rearrangeable.

src.label: Apple — Quick Sampler Slice mode in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Choose a Quick Sampler mode in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Drag audio directly from the Tracks area into a loaded Quick Sampler
tips.d: Drag a region into Quick Sampler's waveform display to swap the sound. Drop it on Original to keep the file's own tuning, loudness, looping and length. Drop it on Optimized and Quick Sampler optimizes tuning, loudness and length, and adds loop and crossfade markers to rhythmic or looped material. The region is bounced offline first. Dragging to the track header instead opens the Replace existing sound dialog.

src.label: Apple — Add audio to Quick Sampler in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Drag and drop to create sampler instrument tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Flex and Follow Tempo to lock a loop to the project
tips.d: Flex and Follow Tempo are separate buttons at the lower right of the waveform display in Classic, One Shot and Slice modes. Flex alone plays the sample at its original speed on every key: the pitch changes, the speed doesn't. Turn on Follow Tempo as well and playback syncs to the project tempo, with slices stretching or contracting to match.

src.label: Apple — Use Flex in Quick Sampler in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Set the root key correctly or nothing will be in tune
tips.d: The root key is the note that plays your sample at its original pitch; keys above and below transpose it up or down. If a sample plays out of tune across the keyboard, open the Pitch controls and set the Root Key pop-up menu to the note the sample actually is.

src.label: Apple — Quick Sampler Pitch controls in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Shuffle the slice MIDI to rearrange the break
tips.d: The generated MIDI plays the slices in the original order. Now shuffle the notes and the break rearranges itself.

src.label: Apple — Quick Sampler Slice mode in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Choose a Quick Sampler mode in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Convert Quick Sampler to Sampler for full control
tips.d: Replace Quick Sampler with Sampler on the instrument channel strip and your current content transfers automatically. Do it when you need to work with more than one audio file at a time. It is a one-way trip: Sampler can load Quick Sampler settings, but Quick Sampler cannot open a Sampler setting.
